adult.title: Adult

rows.group: Linear core (slopes and one-hot offsets), strongest in the data first

rows.name: \textbf{Marital status and household role}: low income likelier outside marriage: husbands and wives sit well below the unmarried
\textbf{Occupation and work class}: executive, managerial and professional work sit below; service and handling work and missing job records above
\textbf{Education (years)}: each extra year of schooling lowers the chance of a low income
\textbf{Capital gain (slope)}: capital gains lower the chance of a low income
\textbf{Age (slope)}: older people are less likely to have a low income
\textbf{Hours per week (slope)}: longer working weeks lower the chance of a low income
\textbf{Capital loss (slope)}: recorded capital losses lower the chance of a low income
\textbf{Sex}: women are more likely to have a low income than otherwise similar men
\textbf{Race}: small offsets by recorded race
\textbf{Education levels}: offsets for single education levels beyond the years-of-schooling line
\textbf{Country of birth}: offsets for single countries of birth, mostly small groups

rows.group: Non-linear: bends and interactions, strongest in the data first

rows.name: \textbf{Capital-gain threshold}: past a few thousand dollars of capital gain the chance of a low income drops steeply
\textbf{Age bend}: the fall with age is steep for the young and flattens or turns back later in life
rows.usual: a single gate that also reads another input

rows.name: \textbf{Hours bend}: short weeks raise the chance of a low income more than long weeks lower it

rows.group: Relevant in the data but in no network

rows.name: \textbf{Capital-loss bend}: bends in the capital-loss effect across loss amounts
\textbf{Census weight (slope)}: the survey sampling weight, not a personal attribute
\textbf{Age $\times$ marriage}: the age effect differs inside and outside marriage
\textbf{Census weight bend}: bends in the survey sampling weight
\textbf{Age $\times$ hours}: the hours effect changes with age
\textbf{Capital gain $\times$ marriage}: the capital-gain threshold acts differently for the married
\textbf{Sex $\times$ marriage}: the gap between women and men differs inside and outside marriage

legend: a single gate that also reads another input

churn.title: Churn

rows.group: Linear core (slopes and offsets), strongest in the data first

rows.name: \textbf{International plan, offset}: an international plan raises churn
\textbf{Service calls, slope}: churn rises with each call to customer service
\textbf{Day usage, slope}: churn rises with daytime minutes (a charge is a fixed multiple of its minutes)
\textbf{Evening usage, slope}: churn rises with evening minutes
\textbf{International minutes, slope}: a slope in international minutes
\textbf{Voice mail, offset}: a voice-mail plan (and its messages) lowers churn
\textbf{Day calls, slope}: a small slope in the number of day calls
\textbf{Account length, slope}: a small slope in account length
\textbf{International calls, slope}: a slope in the number of international calls
\textbf{State offsets}: a separate offset for some states
\textbf{Night usage, slope}: a small slope in night minutes

rows.group: Non-linear: bends and interactions, strongest in the data first

rows.name: \textbf{Day $+$ evening bill}: the combined day and evening bill
\textbf{Service-call threshold}: churn flat over the first calls, steep from 4 calls
\textbf{Service calls $\times$ light day use}: the service-call rise is strongest for light daytime users
\textbf{Heavy day use without voice mail}: heavy daytime use matters mostly without a voice-mail plan
\textbf{Heavy-day hinge}: heavy daytime use: churn climbs steeply above about 300 minutes
\textbf{International-minutes bend}: a bend in international minutes
\textbf{Day $\times$ night usage}: day and night use read together
\textbf{Service calls $\times$ voice mail}: service calls read with the voice-mail plan
rows.usual: a single gate that also reads another input

rows.name: \textbf{Evening usage $\times$ service calls}: evening use read with service calls
\textbf{Evening bend}: a bend in evening use

rows.group: Relevant in the data but in no network

rows.name: \textbf{International plan $\times$ international use}: plan holders churn when they use the plan heavily or barely
\textbf{International-calls bend}: a bend in international calls

legend: a single gate that also reads another input

heart100.title: Heart-100

rows.group: Linear core: average effect of each input, ordered by how many seeds share its direction

rows.name: \textbf{Typical angina}: lowers risk
\textbf{Female (vs male)}: lowers risk
\textbf{Flat ST slope}: raises risk
\textbf{Non-anginal pain}: lowers risk
\textbf{Vessels coloured}: risk rises with it
\textbf{Thallium: reversible defect}: raises risk
\textbf{Age}: risk rises with it
\textbf{Maximum heart rate}: risk falls with it
\textbf{Cholesterol}: risk rises with it
\textbf{Thallium: not recorded}: raises risk
\textbf{Atypical angina}: lowers risk
\textbf{Thallium: fixed defect}: lowers risk
\textbf{ST depression}: risk rises with it
\textbf{Exercise angina}: raises risk
\textbf{Resting blood pressure}: risk rises with it
\textbf{Fasting sugar $>120$}: lowers risk
\textbf{Downsloping ST slope}: raises risk
\textbf{ECG: LV hypertrophy}: raises risk
\textbf{ECG: ST-T abnormality}: raises risk

rows.group: Non-linear units, by family (the inputs that switch the unit on or off)

rows.name: \textbf{Thallium-scan gate}: a scan defect read through a gate, mostly with ST depression
\textbf{Maximum-heart-rate bend}: a bend or gate in peak heart rate
\textbf{Resting blood pressure}: a threshold, alone or with slope, heart rate, angina or scan
\textbf{Exercise angina}: a gate, read with sex in some seeds (for women in one)
\textbf{Age brake}: risk stops rising, or falls back, past an age
\textbf{ST-depression threshold}: counted only past a threshold
\textbf{Flat ST segment step}: a step, read with chest pain or cholesterol
\textbf{Resting-ECG gate}: the resting ECG through a switching unit
\textbf{Thallium scan $\times$ age}: a scan defect read with age
rows.usual: raises risk for some patients, lowers it for others

rows.name: \textbf{Other (one network each)}: ST slope $\times$ age, chest pain, cholesterol, fasting sugar, sex, vessels $\times$ age

legend: raises risk for some patients, lowers it for others
